articleTitle: Research and Application of Variable Working Conditions Control Method for QR Code Scanner in Ultra-High Speed Packaging Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: To address the issue of low accuracy in reading small box QR codes during the variable working conditions of ultra-high speed cigarette packaging machines, a variable working conditions control method for QR code scanners has been designed. This method adjusts the scanning parameters of the QR code scanner based on the machine's speed and the acquired QR code images, adapting to the real-time changes in equipment speed and working conditions. Fundamentally, it enhances the effectiveness and stability of the QR code scanner's information retrieval, improving the stability of the precise association system for QR code information. Results show that the reading accuracy can reach 99.99%, which is an increase of 3.94 percentage points compared to traditional parsing control methods. This technology can provide support for enhancing the stable operation of the QR code association system in ultra-high speed cigarette packaging machines.

articleTitle: Memristor Based Gain-Scheduling Controller for Erbium-Doped Fiber Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: Incorporating memristors into the control systems of Erbium-Doped Fiber Amplifiers (EDFA) plays a crucial role in bridging the gap between dynamic and static gain control, offering a more responsive solution that optimizes EDFA across various operating situations. This flexibility is well-suited for the evolving needs of optical communication networks, where quick adjustments are often essential. Our study has offered important perspectives on the application of memristor-based EDFA control systems for improving efficiency. Through comparative simulations, it was observed that PI controllers based on memristor outperform traditional analog PI controllers due to their adaptability, which results in faster response times within the typical operating power range. The unique ability of memristor to modulate resistance according to historical voltage proved to be an effective method for implementing real-time adjustment of integral parameters and gain-scheduling control. Stability analysis using Root Locus methods confirmed that memristor- based PI controllers maintain robust stability even as memristor resistance varies. Ultimately, our results emphasize the promising capability of the control systems integrated with memristor to revolutionize EDFA regulation, enhancing flexibility, stability, and responsiveness.

articleTitle: Orchestrating Communication and Computation Efficiency in Edge-Based Knowledge Distillation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: With the rapid development of edge computing, knowledge distillation is an effective method to overcome the challenges of training high-performance models with limited computational resources on the edge side. However, a naive implementation of knowledge distillation could cause resource contention on edge devices, specifically in the communication process of receiving distilled “dark knowledge” while simultaneously performing knowledge transfer, both competing for the limited resources. This paper delves into the system-level challenges of resource contention in edge-based knowledge distillation. In particular, we focus on the resource competition caused by the communication and computation processes. To address this issue, we first formulate the problem of edge-based knowledge distillation. Then we propose a method to orchestrate resources between computation and communication in an approximately optimal manner by employing a dynamic resource allocation strategy. Through simulation experiments, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme via evaluating against random and priority-based resource allocation strategies.

articleTitle: Vehicle and Pedestrian Detection in Urban Traffic Based on SSD-DeepSort
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: With the acceleration of urbanization and the continuous increase of traffic flow, using deep learning technology to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of vehicle and pedestrian detection systems has become a practical and effective solution. To address the issues of low detection accuracy and sensitivity to environmental factors in traditional sensor based detection systems. This paper proposes a pedestrian and vehicle detection method for urban roads based on SSD (Single shot MultiBox Detector) and DeepSort model. Firstly, obtain the original image based on urban road videos and perform image preprocessing. Then, based on the SSD model, prior boxes are generated through different feature layers to detect targets of different sizes, improving the detection speed and accuracy of the model. Finally, based on the DeepSort model, the tracking accuracy and robustness were improved by introducing object appearance feature extraction and similarity calculation. The experimental results show that the SSD algorithm has significant advantages in detection speed and accuracy, while the DeepSort algorithm effectively handles target occlusion and intersection, achieving high-precision tracking. However, there are still some errors and missed detections when dealing with small targets or complex scenes.

articleTitle: Networked Radar Anomaly Detection Based on Graph Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: Due to its stable performance advantages, networked radar has garnered increased attention in recent years. To address the numerous challenges of traditional radar anomaly detection, a graph deep learning-based method is proposed. This method models radar scenarios as graph structures and utilizes graph convolutional networks to learn and extract features from graph data, effectively capturing spatial and temporal information of anomalies. This approach significantly enhances detection accuracy and robustness. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves notable performance improvements in networked radar anomaly detection tasks, providing a viable solution for radar systems in complex environments.

articleTitle: TimeNILM: Time-Aware Dual-CNN Model for Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: Thoroughly monitoring the energy consumption of each appliance in a household is essential to assist users in better engaging in power-saving practices. To get per-appliance electrical profile, non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM), also known as energy disaggregation, is a blind source separation task, that decomposes the total household electricity consumption into the load profile of each individual appliance. In recent years, deep learning models have demonstrated superior performance in NILM tasks. However, when encountering an unseen household, the model performance degrades seriously. We observe that temporal information is beneficial for the model generalization ability, as the ON/OFF patterns of electrical appliances follow a similar time schedule across different households. Thus, in this paper, we propose a time-aware dual-CNN architecture for NILM (TimeNILM), which fully exploits the temporal information and employs feature fusion based on attention mechanism to improve model performance. Experimental results on two datasets (REDD and UK-DALE) demonstrate that our model outperforms state-of-the-art models, achieving 8%-27% MAE gain and 8%-35% SAE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">δ</inf> gain for unseen households.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Video Surveillance Anomaly Detection Method Based on Image Semantic Representation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: In this paper, a lightweight method for video surveillance anomaly detection based on image semantic representation is proposed, aimed at enabling widespread deployment on low-cost video surveillance devices. The approach efficiently embeds representations of each video frame and detects anomalies by comparing the similarity between these embeddings and those of normal and abnormal samples stored in a template library. A key innovation of this method is an enhanced lightweight model training technique for image semantic representation, which incorporates specific semantic information into the model's weights, significantly improving anomaly detection accuracy. This approach achieved an impressive 98.7% accuracy on a custom dataset with an inference speed of 9.4fps on the IoT terminal chip K210. Furthermore, an innovative image-to-image generation pipeline for expanding training datasets is introduced. This pipeline generates a diverse set of images with potential anomalies through multimodal understanding and local editing. Additionally, the method features a hardware-friendly and efficient CNN network structure, specifically designed for resource-constrained devices. This structure optimizes parameter efficiency and computational speed, outperforming traditional techniques in both accuracy and efficiency. The proposed method demonstrates superior performance, making it highly suitable for practical deployment in real-world video surveillance applications.

articleTitle: Cheating Recognition in Examination Halls Based on Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: With the advancement of artificial intelligence technology, smart proctoring has gradually supplanted traditional manual invigilation and becomes the dominant mode of examination supervision. However, existing technologies mostly rely on singular object detection algorithms or deep learning techniques, which are inadequate in addressing the complex and varied conditions of examination environments. In this paper, we design a multi-level intelligent recognition system for candidates' cheating behaviors, integrating an optimized YOLOv8 object detection method based on multilayer perceptron (MLP) with the ResNet deep learning framework. This system mines key frames from surveillance videos to precisely capture candidates' positional information and automatically tags those suspected of engaging in cheating activities. Our model's development relies on a custom-tailored dataset, the cheating and normal (CAN) dataset, which includes instances of academic misconduct alongside standard behavior for training purposes. The model's performance is then validated by assessing its effectiveness on real-life surveillance videos from examination halls. The resulting intelligent analysis model is capable of real-time, meticulous tracking and evaluation of every movement of each candidate within the examination venue, accurately discerning the nature of their actions. Our approach represents a significant step forward in enhancing the adaptability and effectiveness of AI-powered exam supervision systems.

articleTitle: Research on Adaptive Vibrating Wire Sensors Data Acquisition Method Based on apFFT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: Vibrating wire sensors convert the stress and strain parameters of structures into output frequency signals. Therefore, they are widely used for monitoring structural stress and strain in engineering projects. Traditional vibrating wire acquisition systems using time-domain frequency measurement methods are susceptible to environmental interference, resulting in significant measurement errors and even measurement problems such as harmonic interference. This paper presents an adaptive phase-matching data acquisition method for vibrating wire sensors based on digital signal processing. Firstly, phase matching adaptive dual excitation is adopted to effectively improve acquisition efficiency and avoid multi frequency interference problems. Secondly, employing an apFFT-based approach for vibration string data collection to bolster the system's anti-interference capabilities. Finally, evaluation parameters for the quality of vibration string data acquisition were proposed, achieving closed-loop control of adaptive acquisition process and data quality evaluation. Through analysis and experimental comparison, the method proposed in this paper significantly improves the anti-interference ability of data acquisition.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of University Emergency Management System Based on QR Code Scanning and Mobile Terminal
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: Students in universities have the characteristics of high aggregation and large range of personnel activities. This paper designs and implements a set of campus emergency management system based on QR code scanning and mobile terminal, which is mainly used for the emergency management needs of universities in special circumstances such as epidemics and floods. Through GPS positioning and QR code scanning on the mobile terminal, emergency management of college students is realized. The university emergency management system designed in this paper has been developed and put into use in a certain university. The mobile terminal applet has been updated 34 times, a total of more than 100,000 basic data of students have been collected, a total of more than 22,000 students have been reported by scanning the code, more than 2.85 million health check-in data have been collected, and the total number of visits has reached more than 8.31 million times.

articleTitle: Reducing Latency for Radio Co-Processor Design with Dynamic Network Stack Offloading and Spinel Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: With the continuous increase in communication demands and the constant advancement of information network technology, the Internet of Things is being increasingly applied across various fields of life and production. Some works give a certain contribution to it, such as Thread. It supports a Co-Processor (RCP) design to enhance the transmission between nodes, combining with Spinel protocol, which is a general management protocol aiming at enabling interoperability between simple and complex devices. However, it doesn't work very well in some scenarios like high packet loss rate environments. We propose a solution that dynamically offload part of the computational tasks between the two chips in the Radio Co-Processor architecture and give an algorithm to optimize a specific parameters in the Spinel protocol to give a positive effect on reducing latency. We evaluate the mechanism with true nodes. It can reduce the latency by about 8%, which is often crucial, especially in scenarios with a large number of tasks.

articleTitle: A Power-Communication Co-Simulation Platform for Real-Time Microgrid Cyber Security Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: The rapid digitalisation process in power system has greatly benefited the large-scale integration of distributed energy resources (DERs), essentially accelerating the progress towards net zero. However, numerous cyber attacks such as false data injection (FDI) attacks are impeding the normal control and operation activities. This paper aims to establish a real-time microgrid co-simulation platform to fully study the impacts of realistic attack events on micorgrid's control performance. Although there exist a large number of power-communication co-simulation platforms for the power system, they are designed to mainly provide validation services for control and operation algorithms and little attention has been paid to the cyber security. In the established microgrid platform, power and communication parts are simulated in Typhoon Hardware-in-the-loop(HIL) 602+ and EXata Network Simulator, respectively, and a dedicated synchronisation scheme is developed and embedded in Raspberry Pis to achieve master-slave data exchange between them. Based on the advanced cyber libraries provided by EXata, realistic FDI and packet drop attacks are mounted against the mapped communication links within EXata. The results indicate that these cyber attacks can severely influence the microgrid control performance including destabilising system states and specific state deviations, further demonstrating the necessity of deploying effective cyber-resilience enhancement mechanisms.

articleTitle: Real-Time Obstacle Detection and Localization for USV Using Stereo Vision and Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: Unmanned Surface Vessel (USV) is widely used in various fields, and obstacle avoidance is a key technology for USV. Accurately detecting the position and type of obstacles is crucial for obstacle avoidance. Active sensors can accurately detect the position of obstacles but cannot distinguish their types, necessitating the use of vision sensors. Therefore, this paper employs stereo vision and proposes a stereo obstacle detection and localization method, based on SGBM and YOLOv5. The SGBM algorithm generates depth information, while the YOLOv5 algorithm detects the position of obstacles in the image. To address the issue of errors in measuring the continuous position of obstacles, this paper uses a Kalman filter to smooth the trajectory. Experimental results show that the proposed method improves obstacle localization accuracy by approximately 38% compared to raw measurements. Besides, considering the energy constraints and computing capabilities of lightweight USV, which cannot meet the demands of processing vision tasks, this paper introduces an edge-device collaboration architecture, by offloading the USV computing tasks to edge nodes, thereby extending the computing capacity and energy efficiency of the USV. Experimental results indicate that the proposed architecture meets the real-time obstacle avoidance requirements of USV.

articleTitle: ASSCM: An Asymmetric Segmented Smoothing Control Method for Cigarette Weight Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: To address the issue of uneven tobacco density on the cigarette rod leading to control imbalance and significant errors in weight, an enhanced method for controlling cigarette weight is proposed based on the asymmetric segmented control approach. A segmented transformation coefficient has been developed to account for the uneven distribution of tobacco density in cigarettes. This coefficient considers the higher density of tobacco on the upper side of the cigarette rod and the lower density on the lower side. As a result, an asymmetric segmented control method has been established for both positive and negative deviations in cigarette weight. Furthermore, a smoothing optimization is applied near the deviation threshold for the segmented transformation coefficients, further enhancing cigarette weight control accuracy. Subsequently, the control algorithm of the weight control system is field-tested and validated at the tobacco industry production site. The results indicate that this technology is effective in reducing the fluctuations in cigarette physical indicators.

articleTitle: Sample Entropy-Based Reconstruction Model for Low-Voltage Arc Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: Arc faults are a significant risk to electrical safety and grid stability because they can cause electrical fires through open arcs and carbonized paths. This study focuses on accurately identifying arc fault characteristics by collecting high-frequency current and voltage data and analyzing them using sample entropy. To improve the analysis, we have enhanced traditional Variational Mode Decomposition by integrating the Grey Wolf Optimization algorithm to automatically optimize parameters and minimize the mutual information of mode pairs. Additionally, an RBF neural network has been used to model arc faults under various conditions, creating a predictive model for short-circuit arcing and carbonized paths. This model, trained and validated with selected datasets, has shown high predictive accuracy and improved training speed, providing effective early warning capabilities.

articleTitle: Skewed Pins Detection of Aviation Connectors Based on Multi-Modal Cooperative Perception
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: Aviation electrical connectors are critically important components in electrical wiring interconnection systems. Currently, connector defect detection relies entirely on manual inspection, which is error-prone and time-consuming. Due to the unique structural characteristics of aviation connectors, single-modality sensors often struggle to simultaneously detect both pins and holes. To address this issue, we propose a 3D skewed pins detection (3D-SPD) algorithm that integrates both 2D and 3D modals features. Due to the low quality of the raw connector data, we propose a connector point cloud enhancement (CPCE) algorithm that combines multi-view point clouds for point cloud fusion enhancement. Based on enhanced data, we perform skewed pin detection. Experimental results indicate that CPCE and 3D-SPD are effective in detecting skewed pins, achieving an accuracy rate exceeding 99%. Our algorithm can be deployed as an AI assistant on the edge device for the skewed pin detection.

articleTitle: Optimization Model and Simulation Platform for Task Scheduling Between Edge Servers in Edge Computing Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: Edge computing has emerged as a popular paradigm to meet the growing demands of time-sensitive and compute-intensive tasks. In edge computing systems, the problem of task load imbalance among edge servers often leads to high response latency, which negatively affects the performance of individual server. Therefore, a well-designed scheduling strategy for edge task plays a crucial role in improving the overall system performance. There is some existing work on solving the task load imbalance problem by scheduling between devices and edges, or between edges and cloud servers. Unlike the existing work, in this paper we perform task scheduling between edge servers, using low load edges to assist high load edges for task processing. However, due to the multiple tasks that are processed on each edge server, the edge server state is complex, scheduling tasks between edge servers is a difficult problem. To address this problem, we consider modeling each type of task to be processed on edge servers as a queue, and formulate the optimization model with the constraint that the sum of edge service time within a time slot is less than the slot length. And then we model the task scheduling problem between edge servers as an optimization model. Since we need to validate our proposed model through the simulation platform, and the existing simulation platform does not support task scheduling between edge servers, we design a simulation platform with edge scheduling capabilities to validate the effectiveness of our proposed model. Through simulation experiments, it is verified that the edge task scheduling policy obtained by our optimization model can well improve the performance of the edge computing system. Moreover, since our simulation platform is modular developed based on Python programming, it can be easily applied to other optimization models. The code for our optimization model and simulation platform is available at https://github.com/AtticusZhang/PyEdgeSim.

articleTitle: Efficient Docker-Based Resource Management for CPU-Intensive Tasks in Edge-Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: Edge-cloud computing integrating the advantages of edge and cloud to provide high-quality services for mobile users is one of the hotspots recently. However, the increasing number of applications brings various tasks with different resource requirements, potentially leading to poor computing performance in Edge-cloud systems with fixed resource configurations, especially for tasks that are heavily reliant on CPU resources. To enhance computing performance, we first characterize the correlation between computing delay and CPU resources for CPU-intensive tasks based on Dockers technology. Then, we investigate a Docker-based resource management framework to handle task allocation, resource collaboration, and configuration for the edge-cloud computing system, where edge servers can allocate tasks to the cloud and purchase collaborative resources from the cloud while adjusting the configured number of Dockers. In such a way, edge servers can maximize their utility while ensuring quality of service. Based on the intersections between edge servers and the cloud, we formulate a utility maximization problem for edge servers that involves the expected allocated tasks to the cloud, collaborative CPU resources, and the configured number of Dockers, which is NP-hard. Next, based on the correlation analysis between the utility of edge servers and the optimized variables, we propose an effective task allocation and resource management scheme by alternating iterations to obtain the optimal solutions. Finally, we conduct extensive simulation results to show the performance of the proposed scheme in maximizing the utility of edge servers compared to other benchmarks.

articleTitle: Fine-Grained Food Image Segmentation Method Based on MS-Mask2Former
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: In the context of the combination of Artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) and Food computing, food image segmentation is a current research hotspot. It plays an important role in food selection, intake and nutritional assessment. The main problems leading to food image segmentation errors are the presence of a large number of irregularly shaped objects in the same category and the overlapping or intersection of edge textures of multi-category objects. We propose a fine-grained food image segmentation method based on MS-Mask2Former to address these difficulties. On the basic network structure of Mask2Former, First, we designed the Multi-scale Enhanced Feature Pyramid Network(MEFPN). This module processes feature maps of different resolutions in multi-scale feature maps separately to capture global and local features, thereby expanding the receptive field of the network and extracting complex features of irregularly shaped foods. Secondly, we propose Semantic Concern (SC) to realize the positional prior. Guided by low-resolution feature maps, the SC module selects regions with richer semantic information from high-resolution feature maps to achieve clear segmentation of food objects and obtain distinct boundaries. The experimental results show that our MS-Mask2Former method improves 2.16% in terms of mIoU, 2.37% in terms of mAcc, and 1.18% in terms of aAcc compared to other representative and excellent methods in the field of food segmentation, demonstrating excellent segmentation performance and achieving SOTA performance on the FoodSe2103 dataset.

articleTitle: A Discrete-Time Markov Chains Cloud-Based Trust Management Approach Model for Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: Recently, underwater wireless optical communication (UWOC) networks gain increasing attention in marine exploration, resource extraction, and other fields. However, UWOC networks are also facing various types of attacks. Most existing trust management schemes focus on the security of network nodes, which neglect attacks targeting links and hybrid attacks on both nodes and links. Considering a clustered underwater sensor network based on wireless optical communications, this paper proposes a trust management approach that utilizes the discrete-time Markov chains cloud-based model (DTMCC). DTMCC features a three-layer trust framework that comprises node-link-cluster levels, where the intra-cluster trust can be assessed by the nodes and links trust cloud and the inter-trust can be evaluated by the cluster head node trust, link trust, and data integrity. Additionally, DTMCC can predict node and link states, which helps restore normal nodes and links timely. Finally, simulation results indicate that DTMCC achieves a higher detection rate against hybrid attacks while maintaining a higher packet forwarding success rate.

articleTitle: SeP2CNN: A Simple and Efficient Privacy-Preserving CNN for AIoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: As convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown excellent performance in various inference tasks, it has become increasingly critical to enable Artificial Intelligence of Things (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> IoT) systems to run CNN-based applications. However, using CNN-based applications in many AIoT scenarios raises privacy concerns. Protecting the inference phase can preserve the user's privacy, which is an urgent issue according to worldwide rules and policies. In this paper, we propose SeP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>CNN, a simple and efficient fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) method to realize the privacy-preserving CNN inference in pervasive AIoT applications. By carefully combining cryptography and deep learning, we compute ReLU with a composite polynomial as the activation function over ciphertexts. To improve the efficiency, we transform the three-dimensional convolution into a two-dimensional convolution to simplify the calculation. Finally, through extensive experiments on multiple datasets, we validate and evaluate the performance of SeP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>CNN.

articleTitle: Defid: Detecting and Filtering Distributed Denial of Service Attack in Edge Computing Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: Edge computing has evolved as a decentralised technology for processing data closer to its source, thus reducing latency and improving bandwidth utilisation. However, this shift also introduces new security challenges, particularly Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks. As there are numerous components associated with the edge computing environment, the effect of an attack on one component can be cascaded to other components which can severely disrupt the application execution. To handle that, this paper presents DEFID, a framework for DDoS attack detection and filtering in the edge computing environment. Defid utilises Extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF) to detect and filter the DDoS attack. Since eBPF allows efficient execution of custom monitoring and filtering programs executing directly within the Linux kernel, it provides a lightweight, high-performance and flexible framework for real-time network traffic analysis. The effectiveness of Defid is analysed using three separate attack programs, Goldeneye, SlowLoris and Tor's Hammer Attack in a test environment which shows that the proposed solution is able to accurately detect and filter various types of DDoS attack traffic with minimal overhead.

articleTitle: Surtify: A Smart Surface Identification System Based on Multi-dimensional Acoustic Dispersion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: With the continuous advancement of the smart home market, household items have become more intelligent. By identifying the different material attributes of various household tabletops, we can obtain contextual information and engage in further interactions. This paper explores a phenomenon, acoustic dispersion and applies it to surface identification. Integrating mobile deep learning, we propose a method to recognize solid surface materials through tapping and utilize tapping events as triggers for interaction by identifying surface material categories. To achieve the goal of zero training effort and tiny hardware cost for unseen users, we analyze the propagation patterns of different frequency components in tapping sound signals from both temporal and spatial dimensions. Based on this, we propose a time-frequency data augmentation strategy that combines multiple event points to improve the recognition accuracy. The results show that, using the leave-one-user-out cross validation for 24 volunteers trained with simple guidance on tapping intensity and position, our system achieves a recognition accuracy of 98.6% for 11 common material types. For 11 newly recruited volunteers without specific control over force and position, the accuracy also remains at 93.4%. We also conduct a series of cross-environment experiments and user study, all of which indicate the high potential of our system.

articleTitle: Enhanced Non-Contact Vital Sign Monitoring via Depth Camera-assisted Millimeter-Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: Non-contact vital sign monitoring with mmWave radar has been regarded as an effective method for identifying lung and heart diseases due to its strong penetration and non-invasive capabilities. Nevertheless, relying solely on millimeter-wave radar for vital sign monitoring is susceptible to interference from multipath reflections, which degrades the measurement accuracy. To address this issue and enhance measurement accuracy, we propose a system design that leverages the depth camera for precise target location and subsequently employs dynamic beamforming techniques to effectively monitor the specified region. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed system achieves an average error of 2.44 beats per minute (BPM) for heart rate monitoring and 0.22 breaths per minute (BPM) for respiratory rate monitoring. Compared to systems without beamforming, our system reduces the mean error for heart rate monitoring by 4.21 BPM and for respiratory rate monitoring by 0.51 BPM.

articleTitle: Multiple Attack Layered Detection Mechanism in Vehicular Named Data Networking
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: Vehicular Named Data Networking is subject to a variety of attacks, including Interest Flooding Attack, On-Off Attack, and Collusive Interest Flooding Attack, which can affect the communication efficiency of the network. For scenarios where the three aforementioned attacks coexist, a multiple attack layered detection mechanism is proposed. The mechanism is divided into two layers. The first layer determines whether there are attacks by self-detecting of vehicle nodes and roadside units. The second layer identifies the attack type according to the location distribution of the attacked vehicles and the network traffic. Simulation experiments show that the mechanism proposed in this paper improves the attack identification accuracy by an average of 20% and up to 27%, and reduces the false alarm rate by an average of 46% and up to 56% compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: LTMVS: Liquid Temperature Measurement with Vibration Sensing Using Smartphones
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: The real-time measurement and monitoring of liquid temperatures is a critical aspect in diverse fields, including food inspection, medical pharmaceuticals, and industrial machinery. Conventional methods of liquid temperature measurement predominantly depend on invasive external temperature measurement devices. These devices are not only inconvenient for daily utilization but also carry the risk of liquid contamination. Smartphones, recognized for their portability and array of built-in sensors, present an innovative avenue for liquid temperature measurement. However, the use of smartphones for this purpose encounters obstacles in the creation of precise mathematical models and the extraction of informative features. In this study, we introduce a novel method dubbed LTMVS (Liquid Temperature Measurement with Vibration Sensing), grounded on the principle of liquid viscosity. This approach employs the smartphone's vibration motor to generate vibration signals and conducts pattern matching on the echo produced by the cup wall, facilitating non-invasive temperature measurement. We executed extensive experiments using the LTMVS system to measure maltose within a temperature range of 32°C to 63°C. The average absolute error was approximately 1.74°C, and the average absolute error percentage was around 3.91%. These results validate the efficacy and precision of this approach in liquid temperature measurement.

articleTitle: Community-Based Robustness Analysis of Cyber-Physical Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: This paper entails the application of the community detection problem and delves into the modularity influence on the robustness of cyber-physical systems. To illustrate this, a widely employed artificial interdependent power-communication network is adopted as a case study, examining various failure scenarios and coupling modes. The DC load flow model and generalized central betweenness model are introduced to model the power and communication network, and a strong interdependency is adopted. This approach allows visualization communities, and the impact of modularity on the interdependent network's robustness is investigated from structural and functional perspectives. Results have shown that damage to inter-community edges between different communities can lead to severe network vulnerability. Accordingly, prioritizing the security of these edges will strengthen the network's resilience, which is crucial for preventing further network damage. We also extend our analysis to examine the impact of three typical network topologies on the interdependent network's robustness, offering insights relevant to the specific network studied and applicable to other interdependent infrastructure networks.

articleTitle: A Model-based Optimization Approach for Through-wall Wi-Fi Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: This paper focuses on optimizing the Wi-Fi sensing ability for non-line-of-sight (NLOS) environments. Existing Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI) based methods are categorized into pattern-based and model-based approaches. Pattern-based methods, relying on machine learning, require extensive training data and are less adaptable to changing scenarios. Conversely, model-based methods utilize physical principles and are more robust, demanding less training data. While most current model-based research targets line-of-sight (LOS) scenarios, effective models for NLOS environments are lacking, where both reflection and refraction are significant. This study introduces the CPR model to quantify the squeezing and stretching effects of Fresnel zones in NLOS scenarios, which enhances spatial resolution. The PASTLBO algorithm, a parameter-adaptive teaching and learning-based optimization method, is proposed to optimize the deployment of Wi-Fi sensing systems by guiding transmitter and receiver placement for optimal sensing performance. Experimental results show significant improvements in sensing performance, with optimized placement of transmitters and receivers enhancing sensing performance by over 30% compared to standard placements. The study concludes that understanding and quantifying the squeezing and stretching effects in Fresnel zones can significantly improve the accuracy and reliability of Wi-Fi sensing systems in complex NLOS environments.

articleTitle: Rate Optimization Algorithm for IRS-Assisted UAV Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: In this paper, an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) is equipped to assist an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) in communication. Our system designed to address the need for widespread connectivity and high-speed services in future urban settings. The UAV in the system faces constraints related to its position, acceleration, and quality of service (QoS) requirements during flight. We propose a method for jointly optimizing the user scheduling, IRS reflection coefficients, and UAV trajectory to maximize system throughput. Due to the complex optimization problem is non-convex, it is decomposed into three separate sub-problems, and then each are addressed using linear programming (LP) and successive convex approximation (SCA) techniques. A closed-form solution for the IRS reflection coefficients is derived. Simulation results indicate that IRS support can significantly enhance system rates, and the velocity profile of an acceleration-constrained UAV shows notable deviations from the ideal scenario.

Index Terms: Speed Of The Unmanned Aerial Vehicles

articleTitle: IMFGR: Incentive Mechanism With Fine-Grained Reputation for Federated Learning in Mobile Crowdsensing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: With the proliferation of portable devices, mobile crowdsensing has rapidly developed. However, traditional mobile crowdsensing faces problems such as single points of failure, data security, privacy concerns, insufficient participation and malicious users. To tackle these challenges, this paper proposes a novel mobile crowdsensing architecture based on federated learning and introduce blockchain to ensure the security of the crowdsensing process. Federated learning, a contemporary distributed machine learning system, facilitates the collaborative training of high-performance models across several devices while safeguarding data privacy. In federated learning tasks, users with elevated reputation values possess a better likelihood of contributing high-quality training data. To this end, we designe a fine-grained reputation evaluation scheme to characterize the behavior of these users. Additionally, to tackle the issue of insufficient participation, we designe a reverse auction model based on historical reputation to attract high-quality users to participate in tasks, thereby achieving fair reward distribution among users with different reputation levels and encouraging users to honestly participate in task execution. A series of experiments demonstrated that the proposed scheme effectively identifies malicious users, attracts high-quality users, and improves the performance of federated learning.

articleTitle: Fourier Series Fitting-Based Intrusion Detection for Real-Time Industrial Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: Recent incidents have shown the attacks against Industrial Control System (ICS), which may result in failure or even catastrophe and prompt the studies of defense. Existing security systems are mostly based on network perimeter defenses which lacking effective countermeasures in the event that such defenses are bypassed and attackers gain access to the system. In this paper, we propose a Fourier series fitting based intrusion detection method, which enables a detection and an alarm when ICS is under attack. Specifically, we first divide the data into three parts based on time with a sliding window, namely real-time data, sliding window data to be predicted, and historical data. Then we fit the data within the prediction window to the data around the window, together with the root mean squared error (RMSE) calculated for the data within the window and the historical data. The intrusion detection system (IDS) will alarm when the difference between the above RMSE and the reference one is greater than a threshold value. We test two types of data injection attacks, extensive simulations illustrate the effectiveness of our method in detecting both of these attacks.

articleTitle: Unbiased Scene Graph Generation Based on Relationship Label Division
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: Scene Graph Generation (SGG) captures triplets <subject, predicate, object> in images, which is crucial for in- depth image understanding and AIoT (Artificial Intelligence of Things) applications. Existing scene graph datasets contain relationship labels with varied semantic information, causing directly trained models to inaccurately infer object relationships. For example, models tend to predict more frequent relationships like “on” rather than semantically detailed relationships like “walking on.” To address this, we classify relationship labels into spatial relationships (e.g., “on”) and visual relationships (e.g., “walking on”). We design two models, Spatial Relationships SGG (S-SGG) and Visual Relationships SGG (V-SGG), to predict these categories separately. By providing the models with different location and visual information inputs, they can focus on predicting the relationship labels they are responsible for. We then merge the results predicted by the two models to generate the final scene graph. Our approach effectively reduces long-tail bias and enhances several metrics on the standard Visual Genome benchmark.

articleTitle: Power Consumption Prediction of Edge Servers Based on Mixed Features and Self-Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: The prediction of power consumption is the basis for studying energy consumption. In previous studies, the functional regression approach is difficult to adapt to current complex server architectures. Moreover, edge servers usually have limited data volume, and it is difficult to meet deep learning demand for large datasets. This paper propose a prediction model based on mixed features and self-attention mechanism, aiming to achieve good prediction performance of the model on small-scale datasets. Feature extraction, feature emphasis, and power consumption prediction are the three-stage workflow of the model. We propose a feature extension sub-layer in the feature extraction phase based on mixed features to reduce the difficulty of extracting temporal features and enrich feature information. The feature emphasis phase aims at selecting the important feature information, as well as further filtering the feature information. A series of comparative experiments show that this model is able to predict the best value of the effect higher than the other models by 26.67%. The ablation experiments verify that the proposed sub-layer can effectively improve the performance of the model.

articleTitle: MineLoRa: Markov Transition Fields and Adaptive Neural Networks for LoRa Device Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: With the development of LPWAN technology, LoRa, one of the typical representatives, is widely used in various communication scenarios. At the same time, it is also faced with problems such as difficulty in identifying the terminal equipment and the easy mistake and confusion. The industry has widely valued LoRa RF fingerprint recognition technology, which has become a security focus that cannot be ignored. Most recent research on terminal recognition has been carried out by multi-class feature fusion. Still, it needs help with high computational complexity, significant noise and other external interference factors, and harrowing feature extraction. We propose a time-frequency feature analysis method based on GAF and MTF. The time-domain features are transformed into two-dimensional images using the Gram Angle field and Markov transfer field. The spectral graph has both time-domain and frequency-domain characteristics, and the feature probability distribution in the images is intuitively analyzed. Finally, we design a deep neural network model based on CNN improvement. It can accurately extract and classify the features contained in multi-time frequency. Our experiments show that a 97% recognition rate can be achieved in an indoor environment, and a 90% recognition accuracy can be achieved in an outdoor environment in time.

articleTitle: FedMSD: Multi-Stage Defense Against Poisoning Attacks in Data Heterogeneous Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a novel distributed machine learning approach that focuses on the issue of data silos and ensures privacy protection. Nowadays, FL research is primarily focused on mitigating poisoning attacks in distributed settings. The attacker has the ability to influence numerous clients and submit malicious gradients. The majority of the current research makes the assumption of independent, identically distributed (IID) data scenarios, which restricts their usefulness in heterogeneous data settings. Current defenses can only mitigate a fraction of malicious attacks, as different defense schemes may rely on conflicting assumptions. In order to tackle these challenges, we propose a multi-stage defense mechanism, FedMSD, which can significantly mitigate poisoning attacks in heterogeneous data environments. FedMSD defends against both conspiracy and non-conspiracy attacks. Specifically, we design a cluster attack defense scheme that uses clustering as part of the defense mechanism, making it applicable to data heterogeneity situations. We utilize absolute and relative similarity metrics to filter malicious updates, thus effectively addressing both collusion and non-collusion in poisoning attacks. In addition, we propose a global security aggregation approach that dynamically assigns weights to the global model based on the clusters' reliability. Comprehensive assessments conducted on two standard datasets demonstrate that FedMSD overcomes current defense approaches and offers strong protection against various attacks in heterogeneous data scenarios.

articleTitle: Doodbot: A Human-Machine Chess-Playing System Based on Edge-Assisted Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: Manipulators have been widely adopted in realistic scenarios like industrial manufacturing, given their many degrees of freedom and extendability. However, under non-ideal environments, the autonomous human-machine interaction of manipulators is still a challenging problem. Moreover, despite numerous advanced methods for environmental perception and planning control, deploying these intricate methods directly to manipulators with limited resources remains difficult. This paper proposes Doodbot, an edge computing assisted manipulator system for human-machine chess-playing. Under the hood, Doodbot makes a geometric model for the manipulator and adopts a model predictive control method to realize the rolling optimal control of the manipulator. Furthermore, Doodbot deploys a hybrid chess-board recognition algorithm combining traditional line detection and convolutional neural network-based image recognition, thus enjoying both the adaptiveness of the conventional method and the high recognition performance of the deep neural network. These computing tasks are offloaded to an edge node in proximity for computing capability augmentation, avoiding long-delayed execution on resource-limited manipulators. The feasibility and robustness of Doodbot are verified through realistic prototype system implementation. The experimental results show that Doodbot has improved the accuracy of chessboard perception by up to 31%. In addition, it can also correctly plan the motion trajectory of the robotic arm and reduce control errors by 36%. A video demo of Doodbot on a real robotic arm can be found on https://ykqm.jyen.top/index.php/s/9q2qH4RajdDffPB.

articleTitle: World Models and Data Governance: Revolutionizing Data Management Through Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: In the current digital era, data governance has become a crucial element for the development of enterprises and society. To address the limitations of traditional data governance methods in handling the rapid growth of data volume, the diversity of data sources, and data privacy and security issues, this paper proposes a data governance framework based on world models and artificial intelligence. By integrating world models with data governance, a modular approach is designed to enhance data processing efficiency and accuracy while optimizing the prediction and decision-making processes. This study introduces a world model-based data governance framework enhancing the intelligence level of data governance. It realizes the application of data governance agents, significantly improving data quality and consistency. Furthermore, the practical applicability of the theoretical model is verified, demonstrating its effectiveness in real business environments.

articleTitle: Physically Secure and Privacy-Preserving Authentication Scheme for VANET
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: The communication between vehicles and other entities occurs over open wireless networks, making them susceptible to various security attacks In Vehicular Ad Hoc Network (VANET). Consequently, many researchers have proposed numerous data transmission and key exchange protocols to ensure secure communication within VANET. The keys and sensitive information involved in these protocols need to be stored long-term in the tamper-resistant devices of vehicles. However, due to the limited resources of these devices, many encryption schemes are difficult to embed. Even if effective encryption schemes can be embedded in VANET, the long-term storage of data in vehicles still carries a significant risk of being attacked. To tackle this problem, we propose an authentication protocol designed for VANET that emphasizes both physical security and privacy protection. The protocol primarily leverages the properties of Physical Unclonable Functions to achieve enhanced security. This approach eliminates the need for vehicles to store keys and sensitive messages long-term, reducing the storage burden on vehicles while enhancing the system's security and efficiency. Detailed security analyses demonstrate that our proposed scheme achieves the goals of physical security and privacy protection. A comparison with similar approaches demonstrates that our solution outperforms them in both time efficiency and communication overhead.

articleTitle: Sensing and Communication Integration Based Fall Detection with Commercial WiFi
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: With the increase of China's elderly population year by year and the increasing number of elderly people living alone, the problem of elderly people death caused by falls becomes more severe. Conventional vision based approaches suffer from some privacy issues to the elderly or guardians. And a wearable sensor-based fall detection methods would leave the elderly constrained and stressed. Therefore, the fall detection technology based on WiFi wireless network has been proposed. This is owing to its significant advantages that it will not cause privacy disclosure problems, nor will it give the elderly any substantial physical bondage and pressure. In this paper, we construct a Channel State Information (CSI) acquisition platform based on regular communication packets with commercial WiFi to perform the sensing via the integration of sensing and communication. In particular, the WiFi works in the commuication mode and sends the comunication packet. The CSI is obtained from the communication package and is exploited for sensing. Then by pre-processing the collected CSI, the feature classification information related to falls is extracted for model identification. Based on the features, the neural network based fall detection algorithm is performed to realize the fall detection. The fall detection system equipped with the front-end interface based on Vue3 and the back-end service based on Python is implemented. The experiment results demonstrate that the system can achieve real-time and accurate fall detection, even when WiFi works in the communication mode.

articleTitle: Proximity Estimation with Position Adjustment for Autonomous Industrial Inspection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: Due to the similarity in appearance and dense deployment of devices in industrial environments, relying solely on machine vision makes it challenging for inspection robots to accurately identify similar devices. Although wireless signals from industrial internet of things (IoT) can serve as identification features, signal fluctuations impact the accuracy and efficiency of recognition. To address this issue, this paper proposes a proximity estimation algorithm with position adjustment for autonomous industrial inspection. The algorithm considers the spatial relationships between nodes and the topological relationship between the signal strength and variations among the nodes. By analyzing the topological relationship between the signal strength and variations among the nodes, the robot autonomously adjusts its position and selects the proximal node based on the spatial topology relationship between them. We have built an inspection platform using quadruped robots to evaluate the effectiveness of the experiments. The experimental results demonstrate that the algorithm further improves the efficiency of identifying proximal devices while ensuring the estimation accuracy of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Data and Resource Management Challenges for Digital Twins
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence of Things and Systems (AIoTSys)
abstract: Digital twins are revolutionizing industries by providing real-time simulation, monitoring, and predictive analytics capabilities. However, their success hinges on overcoming significant data and resource management challenges. This keynote will explore four key issues critical to the advancement and scalability of digital twins. First, we will discuss the complexities of real-time data processing within the edge-cloud-IoT continuum, emphasizing the need for seamless integration and efficient resource allocation across distributed systems. Second, we will explore the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) for dynamic verification of the resilience of digital twins, highlighting their potential to enhance adaptability and real-time decision-making. Third, we will examine end-to-end monitoring strategies to ensure data integrity, transparency, and reliability, enabling trust in automated decision processes. Finally, we will address the integration of emerging computational technologies, such as quantum accelerators (e.g., Quantum Brilliance) and neuromorphic chips (like Intel Loihi and BrainChip Akida), at the edge network to accelerate data processing and improve the responsiveness of digital twins. This talk will provide insights into how these advancements can be leveraged to develop robust, scalable, and intelligent digital twin ecosystems, driving innovation and efficiency in realworld applications.
